definitions.explanation: A pattern, image, or design carved or engraved into a surface — wood, stone, metal, etc. Refers both to the act of carving and to the resulting artwork.

An older / native term for a tattoo, traditionally associated with elaborate Japanese-style designs (irezumi). The term has cultural baggage in Japan due to historical associations with criminals and yakuza, though it is also used neutrally to refer to traditional tattoo art.

notes:
{彫|ほ}り{物|もの} combines the verb ⟦{彫|ほ}る→彫る：00114_horu⟧ (to carve, to engrave) with ⟦{物|もの}→物：02259_mono⟧ (thing). It has two main senses: a carving or engraving on a physical surface, and (especially in older or traditional contexts) a tattoo.

SCOPE NOTES — TATTOO SENSE:
- The tattoo sense ({彫|ほ}り{物|もの} = irezumi) is the older, native term for tattoo, especially a traditional Japanese full-back or full-body design.
- In modern Japan, the more neutral term is ⟦タトゥー→タトゥー：12833_tatuu⟧ (loanword), used for any kind of tattoo.
- {入|い}れ{墨|ずみ} (⟦{刺青|いれずみ}→刺青：09639_irezumi⟧) is another term, often used in legal/news contexts and historically associated with the yakuza.
- Tattoos still carry social stigma in Japan, and many onsen, public baths, gyms, and pools prohibit guests with visible {彫|ほ}り{物|もの} or ⟦タトゥー→タトゥー：12833_tatuu⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {彫|ほ}り{物|もの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{施|ほどこ}す→施す：12985_hodokosu⟧: to apply / put carving on (something)
- {彫|ほ}り{物|もの}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}っている→入る：00494_hairu⟧: to have a tattoo (sense 2); to have carvings on (sense 1)
- ⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{彫|ほ}り{物|もの}: wood carving
- {彫|ほ}り{物|もの}{師|し}: carver / sculptor (or, in sense 2, traditional tattoo artist)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{彫|ほ}る→彫る：00114_horu⟧: to carve, to engrave (also "to dig")
- ⟦{彫刻|ちょうこく}→彫刻：04448_choukoku⟧: sculpture; carving (more formal/technical term)
- ⟦{刺青|いれずみ}→刺青：09639_irezumi⟧: tattoo (legal/news term, often with negative connotation)
- ⟦タトゥー→タトゥー：12833_tatuu⟧: tattoo (modern, neutral loanword)
- ⟦{彫像|ちょうぞう}→彫像：22319_chouzou⟧: sculpture, statue

USAGE:
- In sense 1 (carving), {彫|ほ}り{物|もの} feels slightly informal compared to ⟦{彫刻|ちょうこく}→彫刻：04448_choukoku⟧ (which is the standard art-history term).
- In sense 2 (tattoo), {彫|ほ}り{物|もの} suggests traditional Japanese-style work (irezumi); for a small fashion tattoo, ⟦タトゥー→タトゥー：12833_tatuu⟧ is more natural.
